Solve the supplied rule-constrained task. Return short JSON matching the response schema. Jointly propose an executable rule sketch and any entity/group/usage interface. Do not omit exceptions. A compiled unit needs a source link to a binding or query; unlisted units remain residual. Do not claim unsupported text is compiled. program.kind is expression, connector, or unsupported. For expression body use bindings [{name,value,type,source}], query {op,args}, source_links {unit:[node]}. Types: integer, rational (decimal string), scalar. Connectors also accept relation A string input uses type scalar, not string. Expression names start with n_ for numbers, s_ for strings, b_ for booleans; source IDs such as s0 are provenance only. An expression body requires bindings, query and source_links. Do not copy every source sentence into bindings; bind only public literals needed by an executable query. If no faithful query is available, use unsupported with body {} and keep the native answer separate. {columns,rows,closed}, amount (one value,unit,owner,period,lineage,stage object), amounts (a list of these objects), allowance_bank (entries key,balance,policy,order_observable), resource_key, slot_list. Do not invent entity witnesses or guess allocation policies. A variable is {var:name}. Operators: if,and,or,not,eq,ne,lt,le,add,sub,min,max,scale (literal constant first), divide_constant (literal denominator), array,pair,object,concat. No arbitrary code. Bind observed values and rule constants from public source units. Node names are query and binding:NAME. Use unsupported with empty body when faithful executable translation is unavailable. Always give your task answer in answer; this fixed fallback has no stability certificate. Interface proposals may describe a source-linked join/group/map/reduce graph, but never use source IDs or answers as routing features. Each interfaces entry has exactly fields (allowed semantic field names), graph (connector DSL), and bindings (same source-linked binding format); use [] when unavailable. A connector body has bindings,candidates,source_links,project; optional query wraps its result. Projection modes: identity, amount_value (one Amount), amount_values (list of Amount), entailment_label (Boolean claim to binary Entailment/Contradiction). A wrapper query reads n_result/b_result/s_result, or n_result_0,n_result_1,... for numeric list results. Never bind these output names as public inputs. An expression variable may remain unbound only if public text itself declares its full finite domain: Boolean b_NAME = true/false.; Integer n_NAME in [integers] = integer.; or Enum s_NAME in [strings] = string. Keep its untranslated source unit residual. Other unread text has unknown scope; do not invent domains or missing rules. Do not store case amounts or names as reusable skill constants. Answer contract: object with EC and EV; each is the asset mapping requested in its public view
Executable contract clarification: bindings contain only extracted public inputs and rule constants; never put an answer object or a program into a scalar string. JSON text in a string is not executable. A source identifier such as s0 is provenance metadata, never a boolean or a variable. Read a bound input with {"var":"name"}. and/or/not take booleans; comparisons return booleans. Expression binding names use n_ for integer/rational, s_ for strings, b_ for booleans; numeric references must name n_ slots, string keys s_ slots, boolean references b_ slots. Choose op before writing args. The maximum expression depth is16; use concise expressions. The root query must return the native task result: a numeric operation for Airline, an if producing an Entailment/Contradiction string for SARA, and an object operation producing EC/EV for OpenExempt. OpenExempt EC values are arrays of literal legal citation strings containing §. EV values are arrays of object operations with exactly citation (a literal citation string) and claim_value (a numeric expression). if has exactly [boolean condition, complete true branch, complete false branch]; both branches must type check. add/sub/min/max/lt/le take exact numbers. scale is [literal integer, numeric expression]; divide_constant is [numeric expression, nonzero literal integer]. Arrays use {op:array,args:[...]}; pair is [string key,value expression]; object takes pair operations as its args, never raw JSON fields. source_links maps current unit IDs to existing node names: query or binding:NAME (connector:i for connectors). Use actual cited lines for each input; cite all rule/exception lines needed for the query. Every scalar string must be an exact nonempty substring of its cited unit, never a paraphrase. A boolean binding is allowed only when its cited unit explicitly contains the standalone literal true or false. Assumptions, inferred states and absent information are not boolean inputs. Express rule conditions using comparisons on quoted inputs; otherwise leave the translation unsupported. Do not mark unrelated units compiled. Omitted units remain residual. Unknown semantics must remain unsupported, never replaced with a guessed rule. Interfaces use only the seven documented connector operators, or []. The complete example below illustrates syntax using an invented task. Its answer definition and facts belong only to that invented task. Read the CURRENT public question to determine all required components of its answer. Compile the current public task afresh.

Public benchmark: OpenExempt
[s0] For each asset in the estate, identify all applicable exemptions under which that asset may be protected.
[s1] Your answer to this task must be based solely on applying the provided Federal and State statutes to the given facts. If the task involves a married couple, assume all assets mentioned are jointly owned, with each spouse holding an equal undivided interest, unless explicitly stated otherwise. Assume all assets are held for the personal use of the Debtor(s), unless explicitly stated otherwise.

[s4] 11 U.S.C. § 522(b)
[s5] (1) An individual debtor may exempt from property of the estate the property listed in either paragraph (2) or, in the alternative, paragraph (3) of this subsection. In joint cases, one debtor may not elect to exempt property listed in paragraph (2) and the other debtor elect to exempt property listed in paragraph (3) of this subsection.
[s6] (2) Property listed in this paragraph is property that is specified under subsection (d), unless the State law that is applicable to the debtor under paragraph (3)(A) specifically does not so authorize.
[s7] (3) Property listed in this paragraph is- (A) any property that is exempt under State or local law that is applicable on the date of the filing of the petition to the place in which the debtor's domicile has been located for the 730 days immediately preceding the date of the filing of the petition or if the debtor's domicile has not been located in a single State for such 730-day period, the place in which the debtor's domicile was located for 180 days immediately preceding the 730-day period or for a longer portion of such 180-day period than in any other place;
[s8] 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)
[s9] The following property may be exempted under subsection (b)(2) of this section:
[s10] 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(1)
[s11] The debtor's aggregate interest, not to exceed $27,900 in value, in real property or personal property that the debtor or a dependent of the debtor uses as a residence, in a cooperative that owns property that the debtor or a dependent of the debtor uses as a residence, or in a burial plot for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.
[s12] 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(2)

[s14] 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3)

[s16] 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(4)
[s17] The debtor's aggregate interest, not to exceed $1,875 in value, in jewelry held primarily for the personal, family, or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.
[s18] 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5)
[s19] The debtor's aggregate interest in any property, not to exceed in value $1,475 plus up to $13,950 of any unused amount of the exemption provided under paragraph (1) of this subsection.
[s20] 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(6)
[s21] The debtor's aggregate interest, not to exceed $2,800 in value, in any implements, professional books, or tools, of the trade of the debtor or the trade of a dependent of the debtor.

[s23] Professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

[s25] Subject to the limitation in subsection (b), this section shall apply separately with respect to each debtor in a joint case.

[s28] Homestead exemptions. [s30] Only one homestead exemption may be held by a married couple or a single person under this section. The value as specified in this section refers to the equity of a single person or married couple. If a married couple lived together in a dwelling house, a condominium or cooperative, a mobile home or a mobile home plus land on which the mobile home is located and are then divorced, the total exemption allowed for that residence to either or both persons shall not exceed $400,000 in value.
[s31] Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1101(C)
[s32] The homestead exemption, not exceeding the value provided for in subsection A, automatically attaches to the person's interest in identifiable cash proceeds from the voluntary or involuntary sale of the property. Only one homestead exemption at a time may be held by a person under this section.

[s67] Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130(2)
[s68] Farm machinery, utensils, implements of husbandry, feed, seed, grain and animals not in excess of an aggregate value of two thousand five hundred dollars.

[s70] In accordance with 11 U.S.C. 522 (b), residents of this state are not entitled to the federal exemptions provided in 11 U.S.C. 522 (d).

[s72] 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-901
[s73] Sec. 12-901. Amount. Every individual is entitled to an estate of homestead to the extent in value of $15,000 of his or her interest in a farm or lot of land and buildings thereon, a condominium, or personal property, owned or rightly possessed by lease or otherwise and occupied by him or her as a residence, or in a cooperative that owns property that the individual uses as a residence. That homestead and all right in and title to that homestead is exempt from attachment, judgment, levy, or judgment sale for the payment of his or her debts or other purposes and from the laws of conveyance, descent, and legacy. This Section is not applicable between joint tenants or tenants in common but it is applicable as to any creditors of those persons. If 2 or more individuals own property that is exempt as a homestead, the value of the exemption of each individual may not exceed his or her proportionate share of $30,000 based upon percentage of ownership.

[s75] Sec. 12-906. Proceeds of sale. [s115] Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(1)
[s116] Homestead exemption. A homestead shall be exempt from sale on execution, from the lien of every judgment and from liability in any form for the debts of the owner to the amount in value of $40,000, except as otherwise provided by law. The exemption shall be effective without the necessity of a claim thereof by the judgment debtor. When two or more members of a household are debtors whose interests in the homestead are subject to sale on execution, the lien of a judgment or liability in any form, their combined exemptions under this section shall not exceed $50,000. The homestead must be the actual abode of and occupied by the owner, or the owner's spouse, parent or child, but the exemption shall not be impaired by: Temporary removal or temporary absence with the intention to reoccupy the same as a homestead; (b) Removal or absence from the property; or The sale of the property.

[s152] Homestead exemption definition.
[s153] Wis. Stat. § 815.20(1)
[s154] An exempt homestead selected by a resident owner and occupied by him or her shall be exempt from execution, from the lien of every judgment, and from liability for the debts of the owner to the amount of $75,000, except mortgages, laborers', mechanics', and purchase money liens and taxes and except as otherwise provided. The exemption extends to land owned by husband and wife jointly or in common or as marital property, and each spouse may claim a homestead exemption of not more than $75,000. The exemption extends to the interest therein of tenants in common, having a homestead thereon with the consent of the cotenants, and to any estate less than a fee.
